decisions.statement: A limit refuses, throttles or ends the thing limited, and says which.
A limit nothing enforces is no limit.
A limit is stated where the thing limited is started.
A ceiling above what the host has bounds nothing.
A limit is read against every other limit the same host holds.
The limit a program takes is the lowest of the limits reaching that program.
A limit has a level that throttles and a level that ends.
The level that throttles is reached before the level that ends.
A limit reached ends every process under the thing limited at once.
A runtime's own ceiling is below the limit reaching the program that runtime runs.
A limit states a ceiling for swap as well as for memory.
The memory a host keeps for itself is taken out before anything else is limited.
Every limit is set from a measured peak rather than chosen.
A limit states a share the thing limited always has as well as a ceiling.
The shares one host states add to no more than that host has.
The ceilings one host states add to more than that host has.
Every memory limit is the value of a page property.

definition: the most memory one thing may take, and what happens when it asks for more
